source.title: Born a Transformer -- Always a Transformer? On the Effect of Pretraining on Architectural Abilities
source.authors: Mayank Jobanputra; Yana Veitsman; Yash Sarrof; A. Bakalova; Vera Demberg; Ellie Pavlick; Michael Hahn

record.tranche_reason: The study uses behavioral retrieval/copying tests and path patching to test induction- and anti-induction-head roles, rather than reproducing the original training-dynamics and loss-curve measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work linking induction heads to in-context learning and describes the usual induction circuit, but those citations are not results of this study. It does not measure induction-head formation over training or a training-loss bump. Its own relevant results are in-context retrieval/copying behavior, head attention scores, and path-patching effects on copying accuracy.
record.test_reason: Path patching in pretrained Llama, Qwen and GPT-2 shows that cutting the induction path (previous-token information in keys) destroys unique forward copying. That is a new-setting result on whether induction-type circuits exist and are causal across model families (V4). It does not study training dynamics, the share of in-context learning, or small attention-only models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that pretraining amplifies induction circuits, making rightward/forward retrieval and copying easier, but does not overcome theoretical limits on non-unique retrieval and copying. They attribute the directional bias to induction circuits being stronger than anti-induction circuits, supported by path patching. Task fine-tuning rebalances the two circuit types and restores theory-aligned length generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates synthetic retrieval and copying tasks in pretrained LLMs, measures head attention, and uses path patching; it does not reproduce the original study’s training-time induction-head formation and loss-curve analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Task direction and head family change the effect; fine-tuning changes relevant head strength and copying accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained LLMs have weaker anti-induction circuits (predicting the token left of the earlier occurrence) than induction circuits. Removing the anti-induction path cripples backward copying. Fine-tuning boosts anti-induction heads and removes the asymmetry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining favours induction over anti-induction circuits, producing a rightward/forward retrieval and copying bias that is not inherent to the architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Task fine-tuning on copying strengthens induction-head attention for forward copying in GPT-2-XL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeted fine-tuning amplifies existing induction heads.

record.problems: The mechanistic ablation results are largely conveyed in figures and qualitative text, with no numeric accuracy values for most groups. Fine-tuning experiments use task-specific training, and the paper notes that this component is limited to one 1.5B model. The study covers two open LLM families and does not examine other architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant rows omitted. In-context performance, Lorem-Ipsum copying and Git-history results were not entered as induction-head measurements: the study does not identify the specific head mechanism for those behavioral results there. Training-time formation and loss-curve claims have no measured results in this paper.

untested.parts: No mechanistic analysis of small attention-only transformers. The from-scratch 2-layer models in Appendix B are evaluated behaviourally only.
No training-time formation, loss bump or timing with in-context learning.
No measurement of induction heads' share of in-context learning or of token-index loss.
Pretraining data is not varied. The asymmetry is only hypothesised to come from pretraining, and that hypothesis concerns anti-induction heads.
Few-shot task learning is not separated from copying.

missing.what: Pretrained-checkpoint attention scores showing induction heads stronger than anti-induction heads, with induction heads located in later layers than anti-induction heads.
missing.locator: Figure 7a dashed lines; Appendix E, Figure 26 and layer localization paragraph

record.verdict_notes: The 'removal' of induction heads is a path-patching intervention applied across all heads, not ablation of identified heads. The causal rows are therefore evidence that induction-type computation exists, not counts of heads. The Llama and Qwen checkpoints used in Figure 7b are not named. The V1 mechanism (key composition with previous-token information) is in effect confirmed causally in large models, but V1 is scoped to small attention-only transformers, so it is linked only via V4.

versions.untested_parts: Tests causal induction/anti-induction circuit roles in copying, but not specifically small attention-only transformers or the full formation process in which an induction head composes with an earlier previous-token head.
No training-time measurement of abrupt formation, training-loss bump, or temporal alignment with in-context-learning gains.
Does not test whether induction heads account for most in-context learning in large transformers, or measure token-index loss changes on broad in-context-learning tasks.

Tests head-related effects across the Llama and Qwen model groups and GPT-2 checkpoints shown in its mechanistic analysis; does not establish universality across all families, training runs, other architectures, or modalities.
Tests effects of task-specific fine-tuning on circuit strength and copying behavior; does not vary pretraining data properties or establish when heads first form during pretraining.
Does not distinguish few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or test whether other mechanisms mainly carry few-shot task learning.
Does not track formation sub-steps or multiple transitions over training.

relationships.condition: Pretrained Llama, Qwen and GPT-2 (Figure 7b groups, checkpoints unstated); unique forward copying with few-shot prompts
relationships.reason: Ablating the previous-token-to-key induction path is described as catastrophic for forward copying in all three families (r1, r5, r9). Values are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Ablating the previous-token-to-key induction path catastrophically impairs forward copying in all three model families.

relationships.condition: GPT-2-XL after task fine-tuning on forward copying
relationships.reason: Removing the induction path drops forward-copy accuracy to zero (r13).
relationships.display_finding: In GPT-2-XL fine-tuned for forward copying, removing the induction path reduces forward-copy accuracy to zero.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Unique forward and backward copying in the tested pretrained and task-fine-tuned checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Removing the direction-matched head family damages the corresponding copying task, while removing the other family has negligible or no effect (r1–r18). The study does not directly establish the proposed two-head composition in small attention-only models.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama, Qwen, and GPT-2 groups shown in the mechanistic analysis
reader_labels.reason: The reported direction-specific head-removal effects occur in each displayed model group; the study does not test every model family or architecture (r1–r16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Task-specific fine-tuning of GPT-2-XL on the copying tasks
reader_labels.reason: Fine-tuning strengthens induction-head attention for UF and anti-induction-head attention for UB, and the corresponding head removals reduce accuracy to zero (r13–r18).
